endorsements.quote: By fostering robust algorithmic health literacy, health systems can empower patients to navigate the digital infosphere with critical resilience.
Furthermore, proactive investment must be directed toward training models on diverse, multilingual, and culturally representative datasets to dismantle entrenched Anglocentric biases.

unlisted_practices: Policymakers should establish public-private partnerships to subsidize premium, medically fine-tuned LLMs for marginalized communities and public health institutions.
Policymakers should incentivize academic and open-source communities to develop and validate lightweight, specialized medical LLMs that run locally on low-cost mobile devices.
Health systems should use federated learning combined with differential privacy for medical AI development so raw patient data are not centrally aggregated.
International frameworks should legally classify conversational medical prompts as highly protected data shielded from secondary commercialization.
Regulators should replace static software-as-a-medical-device evaluation with dynamic continuous oversight using predetermined change control plans.

Developers should be required to implement retrieval-augmented generation in public-facing health chatbots, constraining answers to approved peer-reviewed guidelines with citations and confidence scores.
Public health agencies should demand algorithmic auditability of AI systems.
Public health workflows should be designed around human-in-the-loop paradigms, positioning generative models as cognitive extenders rather than autonomous diagnostic authorities.
Clinicians should teach patients to use LLMs safely, including validated prompt templates for symptom inquiries and cross-referencing AI advice with established clinical resources.
Developers and practitioners should transparently inform users that they are interacting with an artificial agent.
Developers and practitioners should anchor all generative AI outputs in verifiable, traceable references to peer-reviewed primary clinical literature.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint / conceptual framework paper proposing an equity-centered sociotechnical architecture for governing generative AI integration in public health promotion, containing no original empirical data.
